title: POC Deployment Strategy: templates and risk matrix
content:
Purpose:
This working doc provides concise, reusable templates and a small risk/impact matrix to guide customer POCs when evaluating hosted vs. dedicated vs. private deployment modes. Aim is to speed proposals (30–90 minute prep), standardize tradeoffs, and produce a one-slide recommendation at the end of a workshop.

Audience:
Solutions engineers, technical account managers, and customer infra/architecture stakeholders running a POC to choose an inference hosting mode. This is intentionally pragmatic — checklists + scoring rubric + sample configs.

Quick decision flow (one-paragraph):
Start with business constraints (data residency, compliance), then scale/latency targets (p95 latency target, expected RPS), and finally cadence of model change / integration complexity. If compliance demands hard isolation or air-gap, default to Private. If low to moderate scale, fast time-to-value, and customer accepts a hosted vendor, choose Hosted. If predictable high throughput plus contractual performance is required and the customer wants Redwood-managed capacity in their tenancy, choose Dedicated.

Scoring rubric (use for workshops):
- Criteria: Data sensitivity, Latency sensitivity, Predictable throughput, Time-to-first-test, Ops burden tolerance, Model churn velocity, Cost sensitivity.
- Scoring: 0–3 each (0 = doesn’t matter, 3 = critical). Sum and map: 0–6 Hosted; 7–12 Dedicated; 13–18 Private.

Three templates (short checklists + sample assumptions):
1) Hosted-first (fast-validate)
When to use: proof-of-concept where speed to test user flows matters; limited to no regulatory constraints; model churn likely in early phase.
Minimum checklist:
  - Sign up + API key, allocate test workspace
  - Define test dataset, sample prompts, and evaluation metrics (ROUGE/EM/QA accuracy as applicable)
  - Set per-route SLOs, token limits and streaming enabled for UX flows
  - Configure fallback policy to smaller model variant for overload scenarios
  - Add billing alert at 50% of trial budget
Sample assumptions (POC): 200–500 users, burst TPS 5–15, p95 latency target 250–400ms (token streaming allowed), cost sensitivity medium.
Risks & mitigations:
  - Risk: noisy production-like traffic causes cost spike. Mitigate: use throttles, sampling in production mirror, synthetic traffic budget.
  - Risk: data residency mismatch. Mitigate: limit test data to non-PII or use private dataset masking.

2) Dedicated-reserve (predictable throughput)
When to use: production POC where predictable latency and throughput are contractually important, and customer prefers secured tenancy but not full private control.
Minimum checklist:
  - Define expected sustained throughput (tokens/sec) and peak TPS for right-sizing GPU pools
  - Agree on autoscale policy (min/max pool size, burst window)
  - Configure model pinning & canary rollout definitions (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
  - Network: VPN or peered connectivity; confirm allowed IP ranges and egress rules
  - Observability hooks: token-level cost, per-route latency, KV-cache hit rates
Sample assumptions (POC): 1k–5k daily active users, sustained 50–200 tokens/sec, p95 latency target 120–250ms, cost sensitivity high but with committed pricing.
Risks & mitigations:
  - Risk: under-allocated pool -> latency SLO miss. Mitigate: trial with burst capacity and conservative headroom (+30%).
  - Risk: longer lead time to provision GPUs. Mitigate: schedule staging window and temporary Hosted fallback.

3) Private (air-gapped / regulated)
When to use: regulated workloads requiring customer-managed network, keys in KMS/HSM, strict data sovereignty, or on-prem compliance.
Minimum checklist:
  - Define control plane topology: detached (customer-managed control plane) vs. connected (VPC peering to Redwood control plane)
  - KMS/HSM integration plan and key rotation policy
  - Deployment packaging: container images, Helm charts, versions allowed
  - Audit & telemetry plan: retention, export endpoints, and redaction rules
  - Rollback plan for model/schema changes, and a manual canary process for air-gapped installs
Sample assumptions (POC): limited user set (internal), p95 latency target 80–200ms depending on hardware, high ops tolerance initially, data residency strict.
Risks & mitigations:
  - Risk: slow iteration due to release cadence and validation. Mitigate: provide a staging pipeline and hotpatch guidance, small-change fast path.
  - Risk: cost and ops burden on customer. Mitigate: offer managed-private ops addon or a hybrid dedicated lane for sustained runs.

Risk vs Impact matrix (short table for workshop use):
- Data leakage: Impact = High for regulated; Hosted = High risk, Dedicated = Medium, Private = Low
- Latency breach: Impact = High for real-time UX; Hosted = Medium, Dedicated = Low, Private = Low (hardware-dependent)
- Cost overrun: Impact = Medium; Hosted = High (usage-driven), Dedicated = Medium (committed), Private = Low/Medium (capex + ops)
- Provisioning delay: Impact = Low/Medium; Hosted = Low, Dedicated = Medium (lead time), Private = High
- Model regression/quality drift: Impact = High; all modes = Medium; mitigation = pinned test sets and rollout gates

Operational patterns and playbooks (practical snippets):
- Canary rollback pattern: keep previous model pinned to 20% for 24–48h; watch error, latency, and quality metrics; automate rollback trigger on defined thresholds (delta > 3% error or latency p95 increase > 30%).
- Fallback policy: define low-cost variant at route level for overload; route policy: try-primary -> cached-prefix -> fallback-model.
- Cost control knobs: per-route rate limits, token caps per-user, synthetic traffic gating, and batching window adjustments.

Artifacts to produce in a 90-minute workshop:
1) Filled scoring rubric (live input from customer)
2) One-slide recommendation with 2 backup options and primary risk mitigation strategy
3) Minimal PoC plan (sprint-style): week 0 onboarding, week 1 integration + smoke, week 2 scale test + evaluation, week 3 decision/rollout path

Next steps template (for solutions engineer after workshop):
- Send recommendation slide + scoring sheet to stakeholders within 24h
- Create an internal ticket: POC-<customer>-<mode> with linked test datasets and alerts
- Assign an engineer owner for provisioning and a success manager for cost/usage monitoring

Open questions to capture during customer discovery:
- Does the customer require explicit data residency or encryption-at-rest keys they control?
- What is the expected burst pattern (short spikes vs. sustained load)?
- How quickly do they expect to iterate model weights or prompt engineering?
- Are there contractual SLAs they need for uptime or p95 latency?

Appendix: sample quick-sizing heuristics (very rough)
- Small POC: 1-2 GPU (A100 or V100 equivalent), traffic < 50 tps, expect p95 250–500ms
- Mid POC (Dedicated): 4–8 GPU pool for 100–400 tps sustained, p95 120–250ms
- Private heavy: depends on customer hardware; try to match memory & nvlink topology for KV cache efficiency

This is a working artifact — use freely in workshops, mark changes in comments, and push refined numbers back to Confluence page linked above.
